# `spirula train` flags

Every training flag, from the table in `src/config/TrainConfig.h`. How to call the trainer, the macro flags and the flags that are not part of this table are in [train.md](train.md).

## Presets

`spirula train [<preset>] ...` starts from one of these. Each row lists the flags the preset changes from the `3dgs` base; anything set on the command line wins.

| Preset | What it is for | Flags it changes |
|---|---|---|
| `3dgs` | Generic method that works well for most datasets. | nothing |
| `360-camera` | Preset for training on original distorted images captured by 360 cameras. Recommended if your dataset contains very wide fisheye images with a circle visible. | `--mask-boundary-offset -0.005`, `--warp-to-pinhole 1`, `--erank-reg 0.01` |
| `in-the-wild` | Preset for datasets consisting of internet images, with extreme lighting variation, with un-masked outliers, and/or shot with long focal lengths. | `--mask-boundary-offset -0.005`, `--center-method focus`, `--outlier-threshold 10`, `--sh-degree-warmup-every 0`, `--noise-lr 10`, `--noise-lr-final 0.1`, `--long-axis-split-opacity-k 0.5 0.6 30000`, `--erank-reg 0.1`, `--means-lr 5e-05`, `--means-lr-final 1e-07` |
| `centered-object` | Preset for captures that orbit a single masked object, whose background is not meant to be reconstructed. | `--apply-loss-for-mask 1`, `--center-method focus`, `--background-mode sh`, `--cap-max 200000`, `--depth-distortion-reg 0.01`, `--rgb-distortion-reg 0.01`, `--erank-reg 0.05` |
| `hdr` | Preserves the dynamic range of the splats; trains linear ACEScg splats by default. | `--background-mode random`, `--background-match-luminance 1`, `--max-screen-size 0.15`, `--ssim-lambda 0.1`, `--loss-saturation-threshold 0.98`, `--dc-reg 0`, `--ppisp-exposure-from-exif 1`, `--image-color-is-linear 0`, `--image-color-gamut Rec.709`, `--splat-color-is-linear 1`, `--splat-color-gamut ACEScg`, `--features-sh-lr 0.0001` |
| `synthetic` | Preset for training splats on synthetic datasets rendered with constant exposure. | `--min-init-fraction 0.02`, `--long-axis-split-opacity-k 0.5 0.6 25000`, `--use-bilateral-grid 0`, `--use-bilateral-grid-for-geometry 0`, `--use-ppisp 0` |
| `meshing` | Preset for training splats for meshing, aimed at the quality of the mesh geometry rather than at how the splats themselves look. | `--primitive mip`, `--sh-degree 0`, `--background-mode noise`, `--depth-distortion-reg 0.01`, `--normal-distortion-reg 0.01`, `--mean-median-depth-weight 0.01`, `--median-depth-normal-reg-weight 0.01`, `--median-normal-supervision-weight 0.01`, `--median-render-normal-reg-weight 0.01`, `--erank-reg 0.01`, `--erank-reg-s3 0.01`, `--dc-reg 10`, `--sh-reg 10`, `--overexposure-reg 10` |
| `academic-baseline` | Hidden from `--help`; still accepted. | `--load-depths 0`, `--load-normals 0`, `--eval-mode interval`, `--orientation-method gsplat`, `--center-method gsplat`, `--relative-scale 1`, `--scale-init 0.1`, `--opacity-init 0.5`, `--use-revised-densification 0`, `--densify-loss-map-mode none`, `--use-long-axis-split 0`, `--max-split-fraction 1`, `--dead-after-epochs 0`, `--max-screen-size inf`, `--alpha-loss-weight 0`, `--normal-reg-weight 0`, `--normal-supervision-weight 0`, `--opacity-reg 0.01`, `--reg-rendered-only 0`, `--erank-reg 0`, `--dc-reg 0`, `--sh-reg 0`, `--quat-norm-reg 0`, `--use-bilateral-grid 0`, `--use-bilateral-grid-for-geometry 0`, `--use-ppisp 0`, `--max-batch-per-epoch 387420489`, `--use-fused-proj-bwd-optim 0`, `--quantization-level 0`, `--means-lr 0.00016`, `--scales-lr 0.005`, `--scales-lr-final none`, `--quats-lr 0.001`, `--opacities-lr 0.05`, `--features-dc-lr 0.0025`, `--features-sh-lr 0.000125`, `--max-steps 30000`, `--use-scale-agnostic-mean 0`, `--use-per-splat-bias-correction 0` |

## Flags

Defaults are the `3dgs` base, before a preset or a macro flag moves them. Tier is what `--help` shows: `basic` always, the rest with `--help-all`.

### Run & Output

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data` | `none` | basic | Folder holding the dataset to train on. COLMAP, Nerfstudio and Metashape layouts are all recognized. Takes a folder. |
| `--resume` | `none` | advanced | Continue a previous run instead of starting from scratch. Point this at a run's output folder to pick up its newest checkpoint, or at one specific step-*.ckpt folder. The model and dataset settings come from that run, while run length, save cadence and viewer settings still come from the command line. Only works if the earlier run was saved with save_full_checkpoint turned on. Takes a folder. |
| `--output-dir-prefix` | `outputs` | basic | Folder that each run's output directory is created inside. Takes a folder. |
| `--output-dir-name` | `none` | basic | Name of this run's folder inside the output prefix. Leave empty to get a name built from the dataset name and the current time. |
| `--num-iterations` | `30000` | basic | How long to train, in steps. More steps often give better visual results with diminishing returns, and a proportionally longer wait. |
| `--steps-per-save` | `2000` | advanced | How often a checkpoint is written, in steps. Use -1 to save only when training finishes, or 0 to never save. Frequent saves cost disk space and a little time. |
| `--save-only-latest-checkpoint` | `1` | advanced | Keep only the newest checkpoint and delete older ones as training goes. Turn off to keep the whole history, which uses considerably more disk space. |
| `--save-full-checkpoint` | `0` | advanced | Store what training needs to continue in every checkpoint, the final one and any older ones kept included. Without it, the newest checkpoint still continues an interrupted run while only the newest is kept. Resumable checkpoints are much larger because they carry every splat slot and the optimizer state. |
| `--save-eval-images` | `0` | advanced | Write rendered and reference images for the held-out views when training finishes. Useful for judging quality, at the cost of a little disk space. |
| `--log-performance` | `0` | advanced | Records the computer and the run once a second while it trains: CPU use per core, memory, disk, GPU use, clocks and temperature, and how long each step waited for images versus ran on the GPU. The files go to the run's perf folder; python tools/perf/perf_report.py with that folder turns them into a report of what limited each stage. Costs a small fraction of one CPU core. |
| `--viewer-port` | `7007` | advanced | Network port the built-in web viewer listens on. Change it if that port is already taken. |
| `--disable-viewer` | `0` | advanced | Do not start the web viewer. Frees a little memory and avoids port conflicts when several trainings run at once. |
| `--keep-viewer-alive` | `1` | advanced | Keep the program running after training finishes so the result stays open in the viewer. Press Ctrl-C to exit. Has no effect when the viewer is disabled. |

### Dataset

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-format` | `none` | basic | Which dataset layout to read. Leave empty to detect it from the folder contents. One of: `colmap`, `nerfstudio`, `metashape`, `none`. |
| `--image-dir` | `images` | basic | Subfolder holding the training images, for COLMAP and Metashape datasets. Takes a folder, relative to `--data`. |
| `--mask-dir` | `masks` | basic | Subfolder holding the image masks, for COLMAP and Metashape datasets. What a mask means is set by apply_loss_for_mask. Takes a folder, relative to `--data`. |
| `--load-masks` | `1` | basic | Use the dataset's masks when they exist, and the alpha channel of images that have one. What they then mean is set by apply_loss_for_mask; turn off to train as if the dataset had none. |
| `--apply-loss-for-mask` | `none` | basic | Whether masked-out pixels are ignored or trained as empty space. Off ignores them, which is how you hide distractions such as people, cars, or the black area outside a fisheye circle. On trains them as empty, which removes the background and leaves just the subject. Left unset, it is on when the only masks are the images' own alpha channel, and off otherwise. Dense point-cloud seeds also default to cut out. |
| `--flip-mask` | `0` | basic | Swap what a mask keeps for what it hides. Masks here are white where the image is kept; turn this on for masks that instead paint the region to remove. Applied before the mask edge adjustment. Only mask files are flipped, never an image's alpha channel. |
| `--mask-boundary-offset` | `0` | advanced | Grow or shrink masks by this fraction of the image size. Negative values pull the mask edge inward, trimming halos and bad pixels along the boundary; positive values push it outward. |
| `--depth-dir` | `depths` | basic | Subfolder holding depth maps, for COLMAP and Metashape datasets. Only read when load_depths is on. Takes a folder, relative to `--data`. |
| `--normal-dir` | `normals` | basic | Subfolder holding normal maps, for COLMAP and Metashape datasets. Only read when load_normals is on. Takes a folder, relative to `--data`. |
| `--load-depths` | `1` | basic | Use the dataset's depth maps when they exist. They drive depth supervision; turn off to ignore them. |
| `--load-normals` | `1` | basic | Use the dataset's normal maps when they exist. They drive normal supervision; turn off to ignore them. |
| `--depth-unit-scale-factor` | `0.001` | expert | Multiplier that turns the stored depth values into scene units. The default reads them as millimeters. |
| `--colmap-recon-dir` | `none` | basic | Which COLMAP reconstruction to read, relative to the dataset folder, such as sparse/0. Leave empty to pick automatically: the reconstruction with the most registered images wins. Takes a folder, relative to `--data`. |
| `--metashape-xml` | `none` | advanced | Metashape camera export to read. Leave empty to find it automatically inside the dataset folder. Takes a file, relative to `--data`. |
| `--metashape-ply` | `none` | advanced | Metashape point cloud export used to seed the splats. Leave empty to find it automatically. Takes a file, relative to `--data`. |
| `--metashape-psx` | `none` | advanced | Metashape project file, used to resolve ambiguity when several images in the project share a file name. Takes a file, relative to `--data`. |
| `--seed-pointcloud` | `none` | basic | Empty uses the dataset's finished dense cloud (dense/roma.ply) when it has one, else its own points; `sparse` always uses its own points. A path: Replace the dataset's seed cloud with an XYZ + RGB PLY in the same source coordinate frame as the cameras. Relative paths start at the dataset directory. Scene centering and scaling apply to both. This is a point cloud, not an already-trained splat PLY. random_init=always overrides it; init_ply uses it only with init_ply_add_points. Resume restores checkpoint splats. Takes a file, relative to `--data`. |
| `--init-ply` | `none` | basic | Start from an already-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY instead of the dataset's point cloud: positions, sizes, rotations, opacities and colors all come from the file. Training still begins at step 0 with a fresh optimizer, and the file has to come from the same photos with the same scene settings, or it will not line up. Takes a file. |
| `--init-ply-add-points` | `0` | advanced | Seed from the dataset's point cloud as well, on top of the PLY rather than instead of it: the PLY goes in first and the points fill what is left up to the splat cap. For a dataset that has grown since that model was trained; without a PLY it does nothing. |
| `--partition` | `none` | advanced | A partition.json written by `spirula partition` or the Partition panel. The run then trains one part of it: the part's cameras, the ring of outside cameras that also see its region, and the seed points they see. The models of all parts are merged afterwards. Takes a file. |
| `--partition-part` | `-1` | advanced | Which part of the partition file this run trains, counting from 0. Required with --partition. |
| `--roi-region` | `none` | advanced | A region JSON: what the ROI editor saves in the dataset's roi folder, or any region (boxes, ellipsoids, cylinders, outlines, half-spaces, a partition's label field, combined with union, intersection and difference). Unset, the first file in &lt;dataset>/roi is used; `off` trains the whole scene; a bare name picks that file there. Splats outside it (see --roi-splat-samples) are drawn for relocation and growth with --roi-outside-weight instead of 1, so the model stops growing there. A partitioned run keeps to where its part and the region overlap. Takes a file, relative to `--data`. |
| `--roi-outside-weight` | `0.0001` | advanced | What a splat outside the region of interest counts for when densification picks where to relocate or add splats, relative to 1 inside. 1 turns the region off. |
| `--roi-outside-opacity-decay` | `1` | advanced | At every densification step, splats outside the region of interest keep this share of their opacity. The ones the images still need win it back; the rest fade until they are relocated inside. 1 turns it off. |
| `--roi-splat-samples` | `4` | advanced | How many points of each splat are tested against the region of interest at every densification step: its centre, then points spread over its Gaussian, turned at random each time. It counts as inside when any of them is, so a splat straddling the boundary keeps growing; at 8, nearly every splat with a fifth of its mass inside does. 1 tests the centre alone. |
| `--roi-mask-pixels` | `1` | advanced | With a region of interest, each image is masked to the pixels whose nearest seed point is inside it, plus a margin, before training. Pixels showing only the outside would otherwise be explained by splats grown in front of the camera, which the merge keeps. |
| `--train-resolution-divisor` | `0` | basic | Train on smaller images than the ones on disk: 2 halves each side, 4 quarters it. 0 or 1 trains at the images' own resolution. The cameras always follow the image files, so a downscaled image folder needs no factor here. |
| `--downscale-rounding-mode` | `floor` | advanced | How each side is rounded when the size is divided by train_resolution_divisor: `floor` never rounds a side up, `round` takes the nearest, `ceil` always rounds up. One of: `floor`, `ceil`, `round`. |
| `--progressive-resolution` | `0` | basic | Start training on smaller images and step up to full resolution as the run goes on, which settles the coarse shape sooner and with cheaper steps. Resolution only changes between full passes over the dataset, so every image is trained the same number of times at each size. Off trains at full resolution throughout. |
| `--progressive-resolution-start` | `4` | advanced | How much smaller the first stage trains: 4 starts at a quarter of each side, then the divisor halves stage by stage (4, 2, full). A power of two, at least 2. It applies on top of the training resolution divisor. |
| `--progressive-resolution-full-at` | `0.3` | advanced | The fraction of the run by which training reaches full resolution: 0.3 is after 30% of the steps. Each earlier stage is half as long as the one after it, since a finer step costs about four times as much. Switches snap to the nearest full pass over the dataset. |
| `--progressive-resolution-schedule` | `none` | advanced | Replaces the automatic stages with your own: step:divisor pairs, for example 0:4, 3000:2, 9000:1. Divisors may only shrink. Each switch moves to the nearest full pass over the dataset. Empty uses the automatic schedule. |
| `--progressive-splat-budget` | `1` | advanced | Holds the number of splats below the maximum until the images are sharp enough to show where more are needed, so the last splats are placed from full-resolution detail rather than blurry images. Automatic raises the limit from the starting point count to the maximum by the same factor at each resolution stage; Manual sets each stage's limit yourself. Off grows to the maximum as fast as usual. |
| `--progressive-splat-budget-schedule` | `none` | advanced | The most splats each resolution stage may grow to: a count such as 500000, a fraction of the maximum such as 0.25, or a percentage such as 25%. A blank box uses the automatic value. Limits may only grow from stage to stage. On the command line: one value per stage, separated by commas. |
| `--eval-mode` | `all` | advanced | How images are split between training and held-out evaluation. `all` trains on every image and reports numbers on views it has already seen. `interval` holds out every Nth image, `fraction` holds out a share of them, and `filename` looks for train or eval in the file names. Holding images out gives honest quality numbers at the cost of a few training views. One of: `fraction`, `filename`, `interval`, `all`. |
| `--eval-interval` | `8` | advanced | Hold out every Nth image when eval_mode is `interval`. Larger values keep more images for training. |
| `--train-split-fraction` | `0.9` | advanced | Share of the images used for training when eval_mode is `fraction`; the rest are held out. |
| `--validation-fraction` | `0` | expert | Share of the training images set aside to watch for overfitting. Training can then stop before quality starts to drop. Early stopping is not active yet: the images are held out but the run always goes to the end. |
| `--warp-to-pinhole` | `0` | advanced | Split each fisheye image into five ordinary perspective views before training. Often gives better quality and wider compatibility for fisheye and 360 captures, at the cost of more images to process. |
| `--warp-spherical-to-pinhole` | `1` | advanced | Split each 360 panorama into six cube faces before training. Turn this off to train directly on the panorama, which keeps the original pixels. |
| `--warp-face-fit` | `uniform` | advanced | Whether the pinhole faces a wide lens is split into all share one size. `uniform` renders them in a single pass, which the fused optimizer needs, and is the faster choice. `per-face` crops each face to the part its lens fills (never under half a frame), drawing 15-40% fewer pixels for less VRAM, but costs one pass per size and turns the fused optimizer off. One of: `uniform`, `per-face`. |
| `--warp-back-face` | `0` | expert | Whether a lens seen past 135 degrees also gets a sixth pinhole face pointing backwards. On a real fisheye that direction holds little but the lens folded over itself, which is usually masked out anyway, and the face slows every step down and takes one more appearance slot per image (about 20% more bilateral grid memory). Turn it on for a lens that genuinely sees behind itself. A panorama always uses all six. |
| `--deblur-training-images` | `0` | stub | Sharpen blurry photos with a learned deblurring model before training. Not supported yet. |

### Scene Placement

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--exif-orientation` | `orient` | advanced | What a photo's EXIF orientation is worth. A phone held upright writes a sideways file and a tag saying so. `orient` reads only the tag, to stand the scene up, and leaves the pixels alone -- which keeps the images and the reconstruction matched for every other tool. `apply` also turns the images as they are loaded, and expects a reconstruction that was made the same way. `none` ignores the tag. One of: `none`, `orient`, `apply`. |
| `--orientation-method` | `up` | expert | How the scene is rotated to stand upright. This only affects how the result is framed for viewing, not the splats themselves. Anything other than `up` is approximated for now. One of: `pca`, `up`, `vertical`, `none`, `gsplat`. |
| `--center-method` | `poses` | expert | How the scene's origin is chosen. Like the orientation setting, this affects framing rather than the splats themselves. Anything other than `poses` is approximated for now. One of: `poses`, `focus`, `none`, `gsplat`. |
| `--auto-scale-poses` | `1` | expert | Normalize the scene so the cameras fit in a unit-sized box. This keeps learning rates and regularizers meaningful across scenes of very different physical size; turn it off only if the dataset is already scaled the way you want. |
| `--outlier-threshold` | `inf` | basic | Discard cameras that sit far outside the rest of the capture. Lowering this rejects more, which helps when a few badly estimated poses stretch the scene and throw its scale off. Leave at infinity to keep every camera. |
| `--scene-center` | `auto` | basic | Move the dataset so this point becomes the origin before training, and record the shift in scene_transform.json in the output folder. Splats are then trained in the shifted frame. Needed for geo-referenced reconstructions whose coordinates are millions of units from the origin, where single precision would lose detail. `auto` centers on the point cloud median when the scene lies far from the origin for its size, and keeps the frame otherwise; `none` always keeps the dataset's own frame. One of: `auto`, `none`, `point-median`, `camera-median`, `camera-focus`, `point-mean`, `camera-mean`. |
| `--scene-center-threshold` | `20` | expert | How far from the origin a scene must lie before `auto` scene centering moves it, in multiples of its own radius (the median distance to its median). The point cloud and the camera positions must both be that far out. |
| `--relative-scale` | `none` | expert | Multiply the whole scene by this factor before training. Raise it when a large capture comes out too small for detail to resolve. Leave unset to let the optimizer cope with scene scale on its own. |
| `--train-frame` | `points` | expert | Coordinate frame the splats are trained in. Only `points`, the dataset's own frame, is supported. One of: `normalized`, `camera`, `points`. |

### Splat Model

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--primitive` | `3dgs` | basic | Shape used for each splat. `3dgs` is the standard Gaussian most compatible with mainstream viewers, `mip` reduces aliasing when views differ a lot in distance or resolution, and `3dgut` handles wide-angle and distorted lenses more accurately and gives cleaner geometry for meshing. One of: `3dgs`, `mip`, `3dgut`. |
| `--sh-degree` | `3` | basic | How much the color of a splat may change with viewing angle. Higher shows sharper reflections and shading as the camera moves, at the cost of memory and file size; 0 gives flat, view-independent color. Values of 4 or higher have limited support in mainstream viewers. |
| `--sb-lobes` | `0` | basic | Spherical-beta lobes per splat, from Deformable Beta Splatting: each adds a sharp highlight that follows the camera, for six numbers. 2 is the published setting. Unless the SH degree is set as well it drops to 0, so the lobes replace the SH bands. Vulkan builds only; viewers that do not know the lobes show the base color. |
| `--sh-degree-warmup-every` | `1000` | expert | How many steps between each step up in view-dependent color detail. Introducing it gradually keeps early training stable and stops reflections from being baked in too early. Small values reach full detail almost immediately. |
| `--background-mode` | `color` | basic | What fills pixels no splat covers. `color` is the usual choice: one colour you pick, and black costs nothing at all. `noise`, `pseudorandom` and `random` all discourage half-transparent surfaces by making a pixel left uncovered land on a colour that changes every step; they differ in how big the patches are, from one pixel to vivid tiles to the whole frame, and the bigger ones the loss cannot average away press harder. `sh` learns a skybox so distant background is represented instead of ignored. One of: `color`, `noise`, `pseudorandom`, `random`, `sh`. |
| `--background-color` | `0 0 0` | basic | The color that fills pixels no splat covers. Black is free -- it skips the blend entirely. Only used with the `color` background. |
| `--background-sh-degree` | `4` | basic | How detailed the learned skybox may be. Higher captures finer sky and distant scenery. Only used with the `sh` background. |
| `--background-noise-warmup` | `2000` | expert | How many steps the background noise takes to reach full strength. Only used with the `noise` / `pseudorandom` / `random` backgrounds. |
| `--background-noise-pre-warmup` | `0.25` | expert | How strong the background noise is at the very start, from 0 to 1. Higher values keep splats from being washed away in the first steps. |
| `--background-match-luminance` | `0` | advanced | Raises the randomized background to a power so its typical brightness lands on each photo's mean brightness, corrected for that photo's exposure. Keeps dark scenes from being plugged with haze to hide a bright background. Only used with the `noise` / `pseudorandom` / `random` backgrounds. |
| `--scale-init` | `none` | advanced | How big each splat starts out. Leave unset to derive it from the point cloud; larger fills space faster but starts blurrier. |
| `--opacity-init` | `none` | advanced | How solid each splat starts out. Leave unset to choose automatically; lower makes early training more forgiving, higher locks geometry in sooner. |
| `--suppress-initial-scales` | `0` | expert | Start splats small where the point cloud is sparse. Keeps them from blooming into large floaters over empty space. |
| `--random-init` | `auto` | advanced | Whether the splats start from points drawn at random around the cameras instead of the dataset's point cloud. `auto` draws them only when the dataset has no point cloud, or an empty one; `always` draws them even when it has one; `never` stops with an error instead. One of: `never`, `auto`, `always`. |
| `--random-init-fraction` | `0.1` | advanced | How many points random_init draws, as a share of cap_max: 0.1 of a million is a hundred thousand. |
| `--random-init-distribution` | `isotropic-gaussian` | expert | What the random seed points are drawn from. isotropic-gaussian is round; anisotropic-gaussian follows the cameras' spread along each of its principal axes; ellipsoid and box fill a solid ellipsoid or an oriented box evenly, sized to the same spread. Cameras all at one height have no vertical spread, which flattens every shape but the isotropic one. One of: `isotropic-gaussian`, `anisotropic-gaussian`, `ellipsoid`, `box`. |
| `--random-init-center` | `camera-median` | expert | Where the random seed points are centred: the median, the mean or the focus of the camera positions (the point their optical axes converge on), or the origin of the dataset's own frame. camera-focus suits a capture that circles an object. One of: `camera-median`, `camera-focus`, `camera-mean`, `origin`. |
| `--random-init-spread` | `median` | expert | How the cameras' spread about the centre is measured: the median or the mean of their squared distances along each axis. The median ignores a few cameras far from the rest. One of: `median`, `mean`. |
| `--random-init-std` | `1` | expert | The standard deviation of the random seed points, in units of the cameras' measured spread. Below 1 packs them inside the camera positions, which suits an object the cameras circle; above 1 spreads them past the cameras, which suits a scene the cameras stand inside. |
| `--use-camera-optimizer` | `0` | stub | Let training nudge the camera poses to absorb small pose errors. Not supported yet. |

### Detail & Splat Count

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--quality` | `medium` | basic | Overall detail level, setting the splat budget and how long training runs. Use a higher level for larger datasets, or for datasets with more detail in them. One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`. |
| `--cap-max` | `1000000` | basic | Largest number of splats the scene may grow to. This is the main quality dial: raising it captures more detail and produces a bigger file that renders more slowly. Worth tuning per scene. |
| `--distraction-robustness` | `off` | basic | Ignore people, cars and anything else that moves between photos. Splats are no longer spent on them, at the cost of some sensitivity to real detail. One of: `off`, `mild`, `strong`. |
| `--min-init-fraction` | `0` | basic | Smallest starting splat count, as a share of cap_max. Raise it when the initial point cloud is sparse, such as synthetic scenes, so training has enough to work with. |
| `--growth-factor` | `1.05` | advanced | How fast the splat count grows at each round, as a multiplier. Higher reaches cap_max sooner; lower grows gradually, which tends to place splats more carefully. |
| `--min-opacity` | `0.005` | advanced | Splats fainter than this get recycled into places that need them. Raising it prunes harder and keeps the splat budget on visible surfaces. |
| `--refine-every` | `100` | advanced | How many steps between rounds of adding and relocating splats. Smaller reacts to missing detail sooner; larger is calmer and slightly cheaper. |
| `--refine-start-iter` | `500` | expert | Step at which splats first start being added. Waiting a little lets the initial splats settle before the count starts growing. |
| `--refine-stop-num-iter` | `2500` | advanced | Stop adding splats this many steps before the end. The remaining steps polish what already exists instead of introducing new splats that never get refined. |
| `--refine-stop-iter` | `14000` | advanced | Earliest step at which splat growth may stop. Growth ends at whichever comes later, this step or refine_stop_num_iter before the end, so short runs still get to add splats at all. |
| `--noise-lr` | `80` | expert | How much random jitter is applied to splat positions early in training. Jitter helps splats escape bad spots and spread into unfilled areas; too much of it blurs detail. |
| `--noise-lr-final` | `0.8` | expert | How much position jitter is left at the end of training. Lower lets detail settle and sharpen over the final steps. |
| `--use-revised-densification` | `1` | expert | Use the improved rule for deciding where new splats go. It usually recovers missing detail faster; turn off to match the original method. |
| `--densify-score-mode` | `mean` | basic | How a splat's need-more-detail score builds up over time. `mean` is the balanced default, `max` reacts to a single bad view, `median` ignores the occasional odd view and helps when people or cars move through the scene, and `geom` sits between mean and median. One of: `mean`, `max`, `median`, `geom`. |
| `--densify-score-blend-world-grad` | `0` | advanced | Balance between adding splats where the image looks wrong and where splats are physically large. Raise toward 1 to spend more splats on big distant structures that image-based scoring tends to starve; 0 uses image error alone. |
| `--densify-loss-map-mode` | `ssim_cs` | basic | What kind of error decides where new splats are added. `ssim_structure` targets mismatched patterns and edges while ignoring brightness differences. `ssim_full`, `ssim_cs` and `loss_full` fold in progressively more of the raw color error. `edge_aware` chases edges in the reference photos whether or not they are already reconstructed well. `robust_edge_aware` does the same but ignores the worst-matching pixels, so moving people and cars do not attract splats. `none` spreads new splats evenly. Any mode with `_nms` first thins the error down to its ridge lines, so splats land on the sharpest edge rather than spreading across the blur around it. One of: `none`, `loss_full`, `ssim_full`, `ssim_cs`, `ssim_structure`, `edge_aware`, `robust_edge_aware`, `loss_full_nms`, `ssim_full_nms`, `ssim_cs_nms`, `ssim_structure_nms`. |
| `--densify-robust-edge-aware-quantile` | `0.9` | basic | How much of the worst-matching image area is ignored when placing splats in `robust_edge_aware` mode. Lower ignores more, which suits captures full of moving distractions; higher keeps more, which suits clean captures where large errors are real detail. |
| `--densify-nms-falloff` | `0.5` | advanced | Only used by the `_nms` error measures. Each of the two neighbours across an edge that beats a pixel multiplies its error by this. 0 is the strict version, which keeps only the crest and can break up leafy, grainy scenes into speckle. 1 turns the thinning off. Values near the middle keep edges sharp while leaving noisy areas smooth. |
| `--densify-loss-map-normalize` | `0` | advanced | Divide each photo's detail error by its own middle value before it decides where splats are added, so a dark or cluttered photo counts as much as a bright, simple one. Off leaves the raw error, and a few photos can then decide most of where detail goes. |
| `--densify-loss-map-clip-quantile` | `1` | advanced | Cap each photo's detail error at this share of its own pixels, so a handful of extreme pixels cannot pull every new splat toward them. 1 leaves it uncapped and costs nothing; 0.99 trims the worst one percent of each photo. |
| `--densify-loss-map-power` | `4` | advanced | Raise every pixel's detail error to this power before splats are scored by it. Above 1 sharpens the contrast between good and bad pixels, so new splats crowd into the worst spots; below 1 flattens it and spreads them out. 1 leaves the error as it is. |
| `--densify-accum-mode` | `avg` | basic | How the error under one splat is turned into its score. `max` takes its worst pixel, so a splat covering one bad spot still counts. `sum` adds the error up, which favours large splats and busy areas. `avg` takes the average over the area it covers, which judges big and small splats alike. One of: `max`, `sum`, `avg`. |
| `--densify-score-power` | `0.4` | advanced | Raise each splat's score for one step to this power before it is averaged over the steps between refinements. Above 1 lets a single bad photo carry a splat's score; below 1 makes a splat have to look bad in many photos before it counts. 1 leaves the score as it is. |
| `--densify-score-clip-quantile` | `1` | advanced | Cap the finished per-splat score at this share of the splats, so a few runaway splats cannot soak up every new one. Applies after the error has been combined over each photo and across steps, and is what the refinement-score view draws. 1 leaves it uncapped and costs nothing. |
| `--densify-final-score-power` | `1` | advanced | Raise the finished per-splat score to this power just before the draw that picks which splats to split. Above 1 concentrates new detail on the highest-scoring splats; below 1 spreads it more evenly over the scene. 1 draws straight from the score. |
| `--densify-oversize-split-fraction` | `0.15` | advanced | The share of each round's new splats spent on splats over the on-screen size limit rather than on the error score. Splitting an oversized splat is what lets it get smaller without leaving a hole. 0 spends the whole budget on the error score. |
| `--densify-oversize-score-blend` | `1` | advanced | How much the error score still counts when picking which oversized splats to split. 0 picks purely by how far over the limit a splat is, which spends splats on empty sky; 1 picks exactly like the ordinary draw. In between prefers oversized splats that also carry error. |
| `--use-long-axis-split` | `1` | expert | Split stretched splats along their long axis when adding detail, rather than splitting them evenly. Gives less blurry distant background in large outdoor scenes. |
| `--long-axis-split-opacity-k` | `0.5 0.6 15000` | basic | How much opacity each half keeps when a splat is split. Given as a starting value, a final value, and how many steps to move between them. Higher keeps the halves denser and sharper; lower encourages floaters to fade and relocate to where details are needed. |
| `--max-split-fraction` | `0.1` | advanced | Largest share of the live splats that may be split in one round, counting revived dead splats first and growth second. Dead splats past the budget wait for a later round, which keeps a burst of deaths from halving the opacity of a matching number of live splats at once. 1 or more leaves both uncapped. |
| `--split-weight-by-renders` | `0` | advanced | Multiply each splat's refinement score by how many times it has been rendered since it was created or last split, so a splat is split again only after the optimizer has had a chance to settle it. The refinement-score view shows the weighted score. |
| `--dead-after-epochs` | `2` | advanced | A splat that no camera has rendered for this many passes over the dataset (fractional) is treated as dead and relocated at the next round, whatever its opacity. 0 turns the rule off. |
| `--max-screen-size` | `0.3` | basic | Shrink splats that cover more than this share of the screen instead of letting them stay huge. Keeps big blobby splats from smearing across the image. |
| `--max-screen-size-clip-hardness` | `1.5` | basic | How firmly the screen-size limit is enforced, from 1 upward. Higher clamps oversized splats decisively; lower eases them down. |
| `--max-screen-size-penalty` | `1` | basic | How hard the optimizer pushes a splat back under the on-screen size limit, per doubling past it. This push is weighed against the photo error, so a splat that has to be large -- sky, a wide flat wall -- can stay large. 0 turns it off and clamps oversized splats on every step instead. |
| `--max-world-size` | `inf` | expert | Shrink splats bigger than this in world units. Set it when huge floaters show up in the distance in large indoor spaces. |

### Image Loss

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ssim-lambda` | `0.2` | basic | How much the loss cares about local structure instead of exact pixel color. Higher brings out fine texture and high-frequency detail; lower gives a smoother, less noisy background, which sometimes looks better in outdoor scenes. |
| `--l1-weight` | `1` | basic | Weight of plain per-pixel color error. This is the main term driving color accuracy. |
| `--l2-weight` | `0` | basic | Weight of squared per-pixel color error. It punishes large mistakes harder than l1_weight, which makes color settle faster but also chases outliers such as moving objects. |
| `--l1-weight-y` | `0` | advanced | Extra weight on brightness error alone, ignoring hue. Raising it favors luminance detail over color accuracy. |
| `--l2-weight-y` | `0` | advanced | Extra weight on squared brightness error. Same idea as l1_weight_y, but large brightness mistakes count for much more. |
| `--l2-weight-u` | `0` | advanced | Extra weight on the blue-versus-yellow color error. Raising it tightens hue accuracy in that direction at the expense of detail elsewhere. |
| `--l2-weight-v` | `0` | advanced | Extra weight on the red-versus-cyan color error. Raising it tightens hue accuracy in that direction at the expense of detail elsewhere. |
| `--loss-scale-min-pixels` | `1920` | advanced | Pick the number of loss scales automatically from image size. Images are halved until the shorter side is near this many pixels, so a dataset that mixes resolutions gets the right amount for each image. Set to 0 to use num_loss_scales instead. |
| `--num-loss-scales` | `0` | advanced | How many progressively smaller copies of each image the loss also compares. Looking at several sizes helps large smooth areas converge on high-resolution datasets instead of only fine detail. Normally left for loss_scale_min_pixels to decide. |
| `--alpha-loss-weight` | `0.5` | basic | How firmly to clear splats out of areas the mask says should be empty. Raise it if background creeps back in. |
| `--alpha-loss-weight-under` | `0` | basic | How firmly to fill in areas the mask says should be solid but the render leaves empty. Raise it if holes appear in the subject. |
| `--loss-saturation-threshold` | `-1` | advanced | Brightness above which a pixel counts as blown out. Where both the photo and the render are that bright in all three channels, the pixel is left out of the loss entirely: both are clipped, so no error there is real. Negative (the default) keeps every pixel. |
| `--loss-luminance-normalization` | `0` | advanced | Divides the color-error weights (L1, L2 and SSIM) by twice the photo's mean brightness, measured in sRGB, raised to this power: 0 leaves them alone, 1 makes a dark capture count for as much as a bright one, and values in between soften that. Meant for training in linear light, where the display curve already makes a dark pixel push harder. |
| `--view-sampling` | `uniform` | basic | `uniform` visits every training image once per pass. `deficit` draws images in proportion to how under-rendered the splats they show are, measured from the splats each image actually contributed to last time, so sparsely covered regions come up more often. One of: `uniform`, `deficit`. |
| `--view-deficit-power` | `0.5` | advanced | Exponent on the deficit ratio under `deficit` view sampling: 1 draws an image in inverse proportion to its splats' render count, 0.5 halves that pull. |
| `--view-deficit-max-ratio` | `8` | advanced | No image is drawn more than this many times as often, or this many times less often, than the median image under `deficit` view sampling. |

### Geometry & Surfaces

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--floater-suppression` | `off` | basic | Clean up floating blobs and see-through surfaces. Tightens the depth and colour consistency penalties and holds view-dependent colour back; `strong` gives the crispest geometry but can flatten thin or genuinely translucent detail. One of: `off`, `mild`, `strong`. |
| `--depth-distortion-reg` | `0` | basic | Encourage each pixel's depth to come from one surface and discourage floaters. Gives crisper geometry and better meshes; too much flattens fine translucent detail. |
| `--normal-distortion-reg` | `0` | basic | The same idea as depth distortion, applied to surface direction. Each pixel settles on one consistent orientation instead of several. |
| `--rgb-distortion-reg` | `0` | basic | Encourage each pixel's color to come from one surface rather than blended layers. Helps discourage false transparency. |
| `--distortion-reg-warmup` | `6000` | basic | How many steps the distortion penalties take to reach full strength. Ramping in lets coarse structure form before geometry is tightened. |
| `--normal-reg-weight` | `0.04` | basic | Encourage splats to lie flat along the surfaces they represent. Higher gives cleaner geometry and better meshes; too high flattens fine detail. |
| `--normal-reg-warmup` | `6000` | advanced | How many steps the surface-alignment penalty takes to reach full strength. |
| `--alpha-reg-weight` | `0` | basic | Push each pixel's coverage toward fully solid or fully empty instead of half transparent. Clears haze and gives cleaner background cutouts, at the risk of less stable training. |
| `--alpha-reg-warmup` | `12000` | advanced | How many steps the coverage penalty takes to reach full strength. |
| `--reg-warmup-length` | `0` | advanced | Hold the depth, normal and coverage penalties off for this many steps. Lets the scene take shape before geometry constraints start pulling on it. |
| `--depth-supervision-weight` | `0` | basic | How strongly AI-predicted depth guides the geometry. Helps in textureless areas, but a heavily biased prediction can pull quality down. |
| `--normal-supervision-weight` | `0.01` | basic | How strongly AI-predicted surface direction guides the geometry. Helps flat surfaces come out flat. |
| `--input-depth-is-ray-depth` | `none` | basic | Whether the supplied depth maps measure distance along the camera ray instead of distance straight ahead. Leave this unset and the lens decides: distance along the ray for a capture wide enough that `spirula geometry` had to split it into pinhole faces, straight ahead otherwise. |
| `--supervision-warmup` | `0` | expert | Step at which AI-predicted depth and normals start guiding training. Waiting lets photometric detail establish itself first. |
| `--mean-median-depth-weight` | `0` | advanced | Encourage a pixel's average depth and its most-solid depth to agree, which pulls splats onto a single surface. Useful when the result is destined for a mesh. |
| `--median-depth-normal-reg-weight` | `0` | expert | Encourage surface direction to agree between the average depth and the most-solid depth. Another crispness dial for meshing. |
| `--median-normal-supervision-weight` | `0` | expert | Match the surface direction at the most-solid depth to AI-predicted normals. |
| `--median-render-normal-reg-weight` | `0` | expert | Match the surface direction at the most-solid depth to the rendered normals. |
| `--median-warmup` | `6000` | expert | How many steps the four most-solid-depth penalties take to reach full strength. |

### Splat Shape

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--opacity-reg` | `0.005` | basic | Gently push splat opacity down so weak splats get recycled where they are needed more. Higher recycles more aggressively. |
| `--reg-rendered-only` | `1` | advanced | Apply the per-splat regularizers (opacity, scale, shape) only to splats that at least one camera rendered this step. Off, a splat nobody renders still loses about one learning rate of opacity and scale per step, which kills fresh splats in sparsely captured regions before their first render. |
| `--scale-reg` | `0.01` | basic | Gently push splat size down. Keeps splats compact so detail stays local; too high leaves large flat areas underfilled. |
| `--opacity-reg-decay-power` | `1` | expert | Fade the opacity penalty to zero over the run, as (1-t)^p with t the fraction of steps done. Its average over the run stays at the value you set, so this only moves the pressure earlier. 0 keeps it constant. |
| `--scale-reg-decay-power` | `0.4` | expert | Fade the size penalty to zero over the run, as (1-t)^p with t the fraction of steps done. Its average over the run stays at the value you set, so this only moves the pressure earlier. 0 keeps it constant. |
| `--opacity-decay` | `0` | basic | Fade every splat's opacity slightly each step, freeing weak ones for reuse. An alternative to opacity_reg that acts on all splats equally. |
| `--scale-decay` | `0` | basic | Shrink every splat slightly each step. An alternative to scale_reg that acts on all splats equally. |
| `--erank-reg` | `0.001` | basic | Discourage needle-like splats in favor of rounder ones. Reduces spiky artifacts and flicker as the camera moves. |
| `--erank-reg-s3` | `0` | advanced | Encourage splats to collapse into flat sheets, so they line up with surfaces better. |
| `--scale-regularization-weight` | `0` | advanced | Penalize splats that are far longer in one direction than another, which suppresses long spiky artifacts. |
| `--max-gauss-ratio` | `10` | advanced | How stretched a splat may get before the spiky-splat penalty applies. Lower forces rounder splats. |
| `--dc-reg` | `0.001` | basic | Hold each splat's own base color -- the part that stays the same from every angle -- inside the 0 to 1 range. Higher keeps surfaces clean; too high clips the real range between bright and dark, so lower it when the scene needs that room. |
| `--sh-reg` | `0.001` | basic | Hold view-dependent color in check so it does not absorb shifts the per-photo correction should handle. Higher gives more consistent color from every angle and better results on unseen views; too high flattens genuine reflections. |
| `--overexposure-reg` | `0` | advanced | Penalize splat colors that fall outside the displayable range. Keeps blown-out highlights from hiding inside the splats, which matters when exporting or meshing. |
| `--quat-norm-reg` | `0.01` | advanced | Keep splat rotations well formed. Guards against numerical drift and rarely needs changing. |

### Camera & Color Correction

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--use-bilateral-grid` | `1` | basic | Give each photo its own smooth color correction, absorbing exposure and white balance drift between shots. The splats then keep one consistent color instead of averaging every camera's quirks. Turn off for synthetic or already-consistent datasets. |
| `--bilagrid-type` | `ppisp` | basic | What the per-photo color correction is allowed to do. `ppisp` adjusts exposure and color gain and shifts hue the least. `affine` is a full color matrix, the most flexible but the most prone to color drift. `loglinear` sits in between. One of: `affine`, `ppisp`, `loglinear`. |
| `--bilagrid-shape` | `16 16 8` | basic | How finely the per-photo color correction may vary, as width, height and brightness steps. Finer grids fix more localized shifts and use more VRAM; coarser is safer on flat, low-texture surfaces where a fine grid starts eating real detail. |
| `--bilagrid-tv-loss-weight` | `10` | advanced | How smooth the per-photo color correction has to be. Higher keeps corrections gentle and global; lower lets them vary from place to place, which can start absorbing real image detail. |
| `--color-shift-reg-weight` | `0` | advanced | Keep the per-photo corrections from tinting the result overall. Raise it if the finished splats come out consistently warmer, cooler, darker or brighter than the photos. 0 turns it off, and 0.01 to 1 is the useful range. |
| `--color-shift-reg-ema-period` | `750` | expert | How many steps the color-shift check averages over. It should be roughly one pass over the dataset so the average reflects every photo. Ignored when color_shift_reg_weight is 0. |
| `--use-bilateral-grid-for-geometry` | `1` | advanced | Apply the same per-photo correction to depth and normal maps. Biased AI-generated maps can then still be used without dragging the geometry off. |
| `--bilagrid-shape-geometry` | `8 8 4` | advanced | How finely the depth and normal correction may vary. Same meaning as bilagrid_shape, for geometry rather than color. |
| `--bilagrid-tv-loss-weight-geometry` | `10` | advanced | How smooth the depth and normal correction has to be. Higher keeps it gentle and global; lower lets it vary from place to place. |
| `--use-adagrad-bilagrid-optim` | `1` | advanced | Use a steadier update rule for the per-photo color correction. Generally more stable and needs less tuning; turn off to use the scheduled learning rates instead. |
| `--use-ppisp` | `1` | basic | Model per-pixel camera effects such as vignetting, exposure and lens color response. Keeps darkened corners and per-photo exposure shifts out of the splats themselves. |
| `--ppisp-param-type` | `no_crf_no_vig` | basic | Which camera effects get modeled. `no_crf` covers exposure, vignetting and color; `original` adds a tone curve on top, and `rqs` uses a tone curve that behaves better in dark areas. Add `_no_vig` to drop vignetting and `_clamp` to clip the result to the 0-1 range. One of: `original`, `rqs`, `no_crf`, `no_crf_clamp`, `no_crf_no_vig`, `no_crf_no_vig_clamp`. |
| `--ppisp-exposure-from-exif` | `0` | basic | Seed each photo's exposure correction from the shutter, aperture and ISO its EXIF records, relative to the set's average, instead of from zero. Photos without those tags start at the average. Helps when exposure varies across the capture. |
| `--ppisp-exposure-arithmetic-mean` | `1` | expert | Center the per-photo exposure corrections so their brightness multipliers average to 1, rather than their values in stops averaging to 0. Applies to both the neutral exposure penalty and the EXIF start. When exposure varies widely, this keeps the splats at the photos' average brightness instead of darker. |
| `--apply-ppisp-before-bilagrid` | `1` | advanced | Run the camera-effect model before the per-photo color correction rather than after. Only matters when both are on, and decides which of the two absorbs a given color difference. |
| `--apply-ppisp-before-color-space` | `0` | advanced | Model the camera effects in the color space the splats are trained in, before the conversion to display colors, which is where a real camera applies them. Takes effect only when the splats use a color space of their own, and needs the camera correction to run first. |
| `--use-adagrad-ppisp-optim` | `1` | advanced | Use a steadier update rule for the camera-effect model. Generally more stable, needs less tuning, and leads to fewer floaters; turn off to use the scheduled learning rate instead. |
| `--ppisp-reg-exposure-mean` | `1` | advanced | Keep estimated exposures centered around neutral. Stops overall brightness from being counted twice between the splats and the camera model. |
| `--ppisp-reg-color-mean` | `1` | advanced | Keep the per-photo color corrections centered, so no overall tint gets baked into the splats. |
| `--ppisp-reg-vig-center` | `0.02` | advanced | Keep estimated vignetting centered near the middle of the image rather than drifting toward a corner. |
| `--ppisp-reg-vig-non-pos` | `0.01` | advanced | Keep vignetting darkening the corners rather than brightening them, which is what real lenses do. |
| `--ppisp-reg-vig-channel-var` | `0.1` | advanced | Keep vignetting similar across red, green and blue, so image corners do not pick up a color cast. |
| `--ppisp-reg-crf-channel-var` | `0.1` | advanced | Keep the tone curve similar across red, green and blue, so brightness changes do not shift hue. |
| `--bilagrid-adagrad-lr` | `0.04` | advanced | How fast the per-photo color correction adapts when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. This rate is constant, with no schedule or warmup. |
| `--bilagrid-adagrad-depth-lr` | `0.04` | expert | How fast the per-photo depth correction adapts when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. This rate is constant, with no schedule or warmup. |
| `--bilagrid-adagrad-normal-lr` | `0.01` | advanced | How fast the per-photo normal correction adapts when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. This rate is constant, with no schedule or warmup. |
| `--ppisp-adagrad-lr` | `0.1` | advanced | How fast the camera-effect model adapts when use_adagrad_ppisp_optim is on. This rate is constant, with no schedule or warmup. |
| `--bilagrid-lr` | `0.002` | advanced | How fast the per-photo color correction adapts. Higher tracks exposure changes sooner but can start absorbing real detail. Ignored when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. |
| `--bilagrid-lr-final` | `0.0001` | advanced | How fast the per-photo color correction adapts by the end of training. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--bilagrid-lr-warmup` | `1000` | expert | How many steps the per-photo color correction takes to reach full adaptation speed. Ramping in stops it from claiming color before the splats have any. |
| `--bilagrid-depth-lr` | `0.002` | expert | How fast the per-photo depth correction adapts. Ignored when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. |
| `--bilagrid-depth-lr-final` | `0.0001` | expert | How fast the per-photo depth correction adapts by the end of training. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--bilagrid-depth-lr-warmup` | `2000` | expert | How many steps the per-photo depth correction takes to reach full adaptation speed. |
| `--bilagrid-normal-lr` | `0.0005` | advanced | How fast the per-photo normal correction adapts. Ignored when use_adagrad_bilagrid_optim is on. |
| `--bilagrid-normal-lr-final` | `4e-05` | advanced | How fast the per-photo normal correction adapts by the end of training. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--bilagrid-normal-lr-warmup` | `2000` | advanced | How many steps the per-photo normal correction takes to reach full adaptation speed. |
| `--ppisp-lr` | `0.002` | advanced | How fast the camera-effect model adapts. Ignored when use_adagrad_ppisp_optim is on. |
| `--ppisp-lr-final` | `2e-05` | advanced | How fast the camera-effect model adapts by the end of training. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--ppisp-lr-warmup` | `500` | advanced | How many steps the camera-effect model takes to reach full adaptation speed. Ramping in stops it from claiming brightness before the splats have any. |

### Color Space

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--image-color-is-linear` | `none` | basic | Treat the input images as linear light rather than ordinary display-encoded photos. `auto` reads an EXR as linear, which is what that format promises, and everything else as display-encoded; set it explicitly for an EXR whose pixels are display-encoded anyway. |
| `--image-color-transfer` | `none` | advanced | The curve that turns the input's light values into the picture the loss is measured on. `srgb` is the plain sRGB encode and is what an ordinary photo wants. `aces`, `filmic` and `uncharted2` roll the highlights off instead of clipping them, which is for scene-linear HDR input that goes far above 1.0. Independent of whether the input is linear -- that is `--image-color-is-linear`. One of: `srgb`, `srgb-clamped`, `aces`, `filmic`, `uncharted2`, `none`. |
| `--image-color-gamut` | `none` | basic | Color space the input images were captured in. `none` takes it from the file for an EXR and assumes sRGB for anything else; `Rec.709` pins sRGB primaries whatever the file says. No tone mapping is applied. One of: `Rec.709`, `ACES2065-1`, `ACEScg`, `Rec.2020`, `AdobeRGB`, `DCI-P3`, `none`. |
| `--splat-color-is-linear` | `none` | basic | Store splat colors as linear light rather than as display values. Leave unset to follow the input images. Linear storage is what switches the color optimizer to its square-root parameterization and trust region; which curve the render leaves through is separate (`--splat-color-transfer`). |
| `--splat-color-transfer` | `none` | advanced | The curve the render goes through before the loss compares it with the photo. `none` uses the input's, which is what keeps the render matching the photographs. `aces`, `filmic` and `uncharted2` put a highlight roll-off in front of the loss instead, so a photo that is nearly white at 0.99 can be explained by a splat many times brighter than 1.0 rather than being pinned there -- dynamic range bought back from an almost-clipped capture, at the price of having to VIEW the model the same way. `overexposure-reg` pulls the other way and should stay at 0. One of: `srgb`, `srgb-clamped`, `aces`, `filmic`, `uncharted2`, `none`. |
| `--splat-color-gamut` | `none` | basic | Color space the trained splats are stored in. Leave unset to follow the input images. A wider gamut preserves saturated colors for later grading but needs a viewer that understands it. No tone mapping is applied. One of: `Rec.709`, `ACES2065-1`, `ACEScg`, `Rec.2020`, `AdobeRGB`, `DCI-P3`, `none`. |
| `--point-color-is-linear` | `none` | basic | Whether the seed point cloud's colors are linear light rather than display values. Leave unset to follow the input images, which is where a reconstruction samples them. The seeds are converted into the splat space wherever the two differ. |
| `--point-color-transfer` | `none` | advanced | The curve that turns the seed point cloud's colors into display values. `none` uses the input's. Where it differs from the splats' curve, the seeds are carried across through the display value, so they look the same on screen. One of: `srgb`, `srgb-clamped`, `aces`, `filmic`, `uncharted2`, `none`. |
| `--point-color-gamut` | `none` | basic | Color space of the seed point cloud's colors. Leave unset to follow the input images. Set Rec.709 for a cloud left in plain sRGB, such as one the built-in SfM wrote with its point colors in sRGB. One of: `Rec.709`, `ACES2065-1`, `ACEScg`, `Rec.2020`, `AdobeRGB`, `DCI-P3`, `none`. |

### Speed & Memory

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--cache-images` | `disk` | basic | Where decoded training images are kept between steps. `disk` re-reads them and uses the least memory, `cpu` keeps them in RAM for faster steps. `gpu` is not supported yet. One of: `cpu`, `gpu`, `disk`. |
| `--max-batch-per-epoch` | `800` | basic | Target number of steps per pass over the dataset, which decides how many images each step uses. Raising it makes each step lighter and cheaper; lowering it groups more images into a step, which is steadier but slower and needs more memory. Datasets smaller than this simply use one image per step. |
| `--min-renders-per-refine` | `0` | basic | Choose the images per step so that a poorly seen splat (at the render quantile) is still rendered at least this many times between two refinement rounds, estimated from the seed points and the camera frusta. 0 keeps the steps-per-pass rule instead. |
| `--render-quantile` | `0.1` | advanced | Which splat min_renders_per_refine protects: 0.1 is the splat seen by fewer cameras than 90% of the others. |
| `--max-train-batch-size` | `-1` | advanced | Upper bound on the images one step may use under min_renders_per_refine, which is what bounds its memory and time. |
| `--split-batch` | `1` | advanced | Process a step's images one at a time inside the training step. Cuts peak GPU memory roughly in proportion to how many images each step uses, and gives the same result as processing them together. |
| `--use-fused-proj-bwd-optim` | `1` | advanced | Merge the backward pass and the parameter update into one operation. Uses noticeably less memory at large splat counts. Not available with `split_batch`, where it is silently turned off. |
| `--packed` | `1` | advanced | Store projection results compactly. Cuts GPU memory when many images are processed per step, sometimes at a small speed cost. |
| `--quantization-level` | `1` | advanced | How compactly colors are stored during training. 1 roughly halves the memory spent on view-dependent color, and keeps the full-size images between rendering and the loss at half precision, with little visible difference; 0 keeps full precision. |
| `--bin-tile-size` | `0` | expert | Edge in pixels of the tiles splats are sorted into, a power of two from 8 to 128. Larger tiles produce far fewer splat-tile pairs, so sorting gets faster and uses much less memory, but each tile then rasterizes a longer list. 0 picks a size from the splat sizes actually measured, and coarsens further by itself when a batch's intersections would otherwise overflow or not fit. |
| `--preallocate-splat-tensors` | `1` | expert | Reserve memory for the maximum splat count up front. Avoids running out of GPU memory partway through as splats are added, at the cost of holding that memory from the start. |
| `--optimizer-offload` | `none` | stub | Move optimizer state to system memory to free up GPU memory. Not supported yet. One of: `sh`, `all`, `none`. |
| `--use-bvh` | `0` | stub | Use a spatial index for splat-tile intersection, which can help when batching many small patches. Not supported yet. |

### Learning Rates

| Flag | Default | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--means-lr` | `0.000128` | basic | How fast splats move through space. Higher rearranges geometry quickly but can jitter and blur; lower stays closer to the starting point cloud. |
| `--means-lr-final` | `1.6e-06` | basic | How fast splats move by the end of training. Positions ease to a stop so detail can settle. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--scales-lr` | `0.02` | basic | How fast splats change size. Higher adapts coverage quickly; lower keeps sizes near where they started. |
| `--scales-lr-final` | `0.005` | basic | How fast splats change size by the end of training. Set to none to keep the rate constant. |
| `--quats-lr` | `0.0015` | basic | How fast splats rotate, which sets how quickly they align themselves to surfaces. |
| `--opacities-lr` | `0.025` | basic | How fast splat transparency changes. Higher clears haze and prunes faint splats sooner; lower gives weak structure more time to prove itself. |
| `--features-dc-lr` | `0.005` | basic | How fast the base color of a splat changes. |
| `--features-sh-lr` | `0.00025` | basic | How fast view-dependent color changes. Kept well below the base color rate so reflections do not run away with the color. |
| `--features-sb-lr` | `0.0025` | basic | How fast the spherical-beta lobes change. Their color, direction and sharpness share this rate. |
| `--background-dc-lr` | `0.0025` | advanced | How fast the skybox base color changes. Only used with the `sh` background. |
| `--background-sh-lr` | `0.0005` | advanced | How fast skybox detail changes. Only used with the `sh` background. |
| `--max-steps` | `none` | advanced | Length of the learning-rate schedule, in steps. Leave unset to match num_iterations. Set it to keep the rates on their usual curve when training longer or shorter than the schedule was designed for. |
| `--use-scale-agnostic-mean` | `1` | expert | Make how fast splats move independent of how large the scene is, so one setting works across datasets. Turn off to have it scale with the scene, matching the original 3DGS behavior. |
| `--use-per-splat-bias-correction` | `1` | expert | Give newly created splats a fresh start in the optimizer. They then move at full speed instead of inheriting the momentum of the splat they came from, so new detail sharpens up faster. |
